title: N+1 database query loop inside user order processing
diff:
@@ -1,9 +1,6 @@
 def load_user_summaries(db, user_ids: list[int]) -> list[dict]:
     summaries = []
-    orders = db.query(Order).filter(Order.user_id.in_(user_ids)).all()
-    orders_by_user = {}
-    for o in orders:
-        orders_by_user.setdefault(o.user_id, []).append(o)
     for uid in user_ids:
-        summaries.append({"user_id": uid, "orders": orders_by_user.get(uid, [])})
+        user_orders = db.query(Order).filter_by(user_id=uid).all()
+        summaries.append({"user_id": uid, "orders": user_orders})
     return summaries

ground_truth.description: Executing database queries inside a loop creates an N+1 query performance bottleneck.
